svg.text: PDSA + QI tools + the audit cycle

g.text: PLAN
aim + measure
+ change idea
DO
pilot SMALL
1 bay, 2 weeks
STUDY
data vs aim
run chart
ACT
adopt/adapt
/abandon
FISHBONE (6 bones): People · Process · Place/equipment · Protocols · Products/drugs ·
Pressure (workload) — brainstorm every fall/error/infection onto bones, then vote top 3.
5 WHYS (drill to root): \"Fall at 02:00\" → why? dark + no bell → why? bell broken 3 weeks →
why? reported verbally only → why? no maintenance log → why? nobody owns it → FIX: log +
owner + weekly check. Symptoms seduce; roots cure — treat roots, symptoms starve.
MEASURE: run charts + Pareto — plot weekly (falls, infections, waits) as dots over
time (median line; shifts/trends = real change, wobbles = noise); Pareto: 20% of causes
drive 80% of harm — fix the tall bars first. Aim SMART: \"cut Bay B falls 50% in 90 days\".
AUDIT CYCLE (close every loop): set standard (protocol/guideline) → measure practice
→ compare (gap = %) → change (ONE fix, owned, dated) → RE-AUDIT (same tool, same place)
→ sustain (protocol + induction + spot-checks) → publish (ward board + meeting + CPD).
Unaudited changes evaporate; un-re-audited audits decorate. Audit topics: hand hygiene,
drug-chart completeness, partograph use, triage waits, documentation (PRO-I 8 rules),
discharge teaching, vital-sign frequency. Sample 20–30 (enough to act, small enough to
finish); blame-free (systems, not names — or data dies).
SPREAD + SUSTAIN: pilot → prove (data!) → package (1-page protocol + training) →
spread (bay → ward → hospital, champions each site) → sustain (induction, audits, board
visibility, celebrate streaks). Quality dimensions (IOM/STEEEP): Safe, Timely, Effective,
Efficient, Equitable, Patient-centred — every project should lift at least two.
Change ideas need owners + dates + measures — \"someone should…\" improves nothing.
Exam line: \"diagnose with bones and whys, test with PDSA, prove with run charts, lock with re-audit.\"
